slides.title: Shader, vertex shader, fragment shader
slides.source: Source: Chapter 6, “A shader is a small program the GPU runs many times at once”; glossary, Shaders and materials; glossary, Shader foundations.
slides.notes: Grid of 24 by 16 pixels: colour is computed from position. Vertex wave: 70 px amplitude, phase 0.8 per vertex. Disc: pixels whose centres are within 7 cells of the middle.
slides.picture: A 24 by 16 grid of pixels coloured by one function of position, then a row of nine vertices displaced by a sine wave, then a disc of pixels coloured one at a time.

new_texts: A small program on the graphics processor, run many times at once.
ONE PROGRAM, ONE RUN PER PIXEL
color = f(u, v): 384 cells, 384 runs of one program
No run reads another run's result.
A shader is one small program. The graphics processor runs it once for every pixel, all at once.
all_texts: A small program on the graphics processor, run many times at once.
ONE PROGRAM, ONE RUN PER PIXEL
color = f(u, v): 384 cells, 384 runs of one program
No run reads another run's result.
A shader is one small program. The graphics processor runs it once for every pixel, all at once.

new_texts: Runs per vertex; sets positions (waves, displacement).
ONE RUN PER VERTEX: 9 VERTICES, 9 RUNS
vertex 4 is −4.1 px from its base
Positions change; no pixel colour is decided here.
The vertex shader runs per vertex and decides where each corner lands.

new_texts: Runs per pixel; sets colour (tint, glint).
ONE RUN PER PIXEL THE MESH COVERS
The fragment shader runs for each pixel the mesh covers and decides its colour.

slides.title: The pipeline: two stages you write, two built in
slides.notes: Stage list is the standard four; the glossary rows are Programmable stage, Fixed-function and Rasterization. The triangle and its covered cells are computed by testing cell centres.
slides.picture: Four stages one under another: vertex shader, rasterization, fragment shader, blending. Then a triangle turned into the grid cells it covers. Then one vertex shader followed by fragment shaders A, B and C, to show that there can be several.

new_texts: A pipeline step you write a shader for.
you write it; can be several
2 of 4 stages are yours: the two shaders.
Two stages are programmable: a shader replaces them. They are the vertex and the fragment stage.

new_texts: Old hardware steps that could be configured but not programmed.
2 of 4 are built in. You set options, not code.

89 of 384 cell centres are inside: 89 fragments

slides.title: Fragment, varying, interpolation
slides.source: Source: glossary, Shaders and materials; glossary, Shader foundations.
slides.notes: Weights are barycentric coordinates of each cell centre in the triangle; colour = weighted sum of the three corner colours.

new_texts: A candidate pixel colour produced by rasterization for one covered screen position.
EACH COVERED CELL IS A FRAGMENT
89 fragments, each waiting for a colour
Rasterization hands the fragment stage one candidate pixel for each covered cell.

slides.title: The Godot shading language and compile errors
slides.source: Source: Chapter 6, “How Godot compiles your shader, and what a headless run can see”; glossary, Shader verification (Compile error).
slides.notes: The scan checks that each code line ends with a semicolon, brace or closing brace. The log, empty uniform list and exit code 0 are the chapter’s headless findings.
slides.picture: A five-line shader with notes, then the same shader with a semicolon removed and the error log that follows, then the three facts the run still reports.

new_texts: Based on GLSL but simplified; the ideas carry over between dialects.
A GODOT SHADER, LINE BY LINE
Types like float and vec4 and uniform come from GLSL.
COLOR and fragment() are Godot's own names.
The ideas carry over to other shader dialects.
The Godot shading language is based on GLSL but simplified. Same ideas, a smaller dialect.

Same UV on any size of quad reads the same texel.
UV says where on the surface a pixel is. It runs 0 to 1 across the surface, whatever its size.

CLAWD'S BODY COLOUR WITH ALPHA FALLING AND RISING
RGBA is the colour plus an alpha channel. Alpha 1 is solid and alpha 0 is see-through.

new_texts: sRGB is the encoding for images shown to people; linear values are proportional to light, the right space for maths.
Half way up the encoded scale is only about a fifth of the light.
sRGB spaces its steps for eyes. Light adds up in linear, so colours are decoded before the maths.

slides.title: mix, step, smoothstep, clamp
slides.source: Source: glossary, Shader foundations; Godot shading language reference (step, smoothstep, clamp).
slides.notes: Each curve is drawn from its formula: smoothstep is t · t · (3 − 2t) with t = clamp((x − e0) / (e1 − e0), 0, 1).
slides.picture: A plot of each function in turn with a probe moving along it and the output shown as a dark to red strip.

new_texts: Blend two values by a fraction; also called lerp.

all_texts: Blend two values by a fraction; also called lerp.

new_texts: Gives 0 below the edge and 1 from the edge up: a hard switch.

new_texts: Does this run per vertex or per pixel?
Does it compile, with no SHADER ERROR in the log?
Is each uniform spelled the same in code and shader?
Is the range enforced in code, not only by hint_range?
Are colours marked source_color, with the maths in linear?
Which rules does a machine prove, and which need my eyes?
Then say it exactly: not “make it glow”, but “smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, d)”.
